findings.location: analysis/paper_assets/__main__.py:76 + analysis/paper_assets/spectra.py:1804 (affects iclr_manuscript/numbers_v2.tex, numbers_v2_spectra.tex, tables_v2/spectra_*.tex, figures_iclr/spectra/*.pdf)
findings.issue: `python -m paper_assets` does NOT re-run cleanly: the `spectra` module aborts every time with `TypeError: build() got an unexpected keyword argument 'dry_run'`. `__main__.main()` calls `mod.build(root=..., dry_run=args.dry_run, **what)` but `spectra.build(root=None, figures=True, tables=True, numbers=True, data=None, verbose=True)` has no `dry_run` parameter. Command exits 1. Consequence: the entire spectra layer — 13 figures, 5 tables (spectra_mechanism, spectra_mechanism_main, spectra_probe_energy, spectra_probe_widths, spectra_low4) and numbers_v2_spectra.tex (149 macros, 32 used in the tex) — is NOT regenerated, so a later refresh of the CIFAR-CE re-selection silently leaves §4.2's and App. O's spectra numbers stale while the other 53 files update. `common.write_numbers_index()` then rewrites numbers_v2.tex from whatever module files exist; in a tree where numbers_v2_spectra.tex is absent it drops the `\input{numbers_v2_spectra}` line entirely (I reproduced this), which breaks the build. This directly violates PAPER_CONTRACTS' "ONE re-runnable script … one command must update the paper".
findings.suggested_fix: Add `dry_run=False` to `spectra.build()`'s signature (and honour it, as main.py/large.py/reviewer.py do). Then re-run `cd analysis && ../.venv/bin/python -m paper_assets` and confirm exit 0 and `spectra figures=13 tables=5 macros=149`. Everything else reproduces byte-identically (53/53 files, 0 changed macro values), so this is the only blocker to the refresh contract.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/sections_v2/app_profiling.tex:34-36 — caption of Figure 39 (fig:cost_memory, p83), cited from main text §4.2
findings.issue: Caption says the figure runs "over five architectures spanning \numToyParams{} to $163$ million parameters". The plotted x axis ends just past 1.1e7: the five x positions are 593/673 ("MLP (1D, poly)"), 27,562 ("MLP (MNIST)"), 826,368 (nanoGPT) and 11,181,642 (ResNet18). GPT-2-small (163,109,376 params, tab:models) is not in the figure — there is no point, no axis tick and no group label beyond ResNet18. The caption overstates the measured range by a factor of ~15, on the figure the main text cites as the evidence for the paper's central efficiency claim. "163" is also hand-typed rather than a macro (as is "11 million" at app_profiling.tex:26 and app_cifar.tex:23, and "128\times128" at app_cifar.tex:21), so nothing would catch the drift on a refresh.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to "…spanning \numToyParams{} to \numCifarParams{} parameters" (or add the GPT-2 point, which the timing pass has: numGptTwoSvenMsStep / numGptTwoSvenMemMb exist). Replace every hand-typed parameter count in prose and captions with the corresponding macro.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/sections_v2/app_cifar.tex:17 and :19 (macros numCifarLRBestAcc, numCifarCEBestAcc; generated at analysis/paper_assets/large.py:1795)
findings.issue:
A number is attributed to the wrong method. `large.py:1795` defines `num{key}BestAcc = 100 * acc.max()` — the field MAXIMUM accuracy — while `BestName`/`BestVal` are the best method by validation LOSS. App. J then writes "against 
umCifarLRBestName{}'s 
umCifarLRBestVal{} and 
umCifarLRBestAcc{}\%", which renders "against MuonW's 0.3357 and 77.9%". Table 32 on p47 shows MuonW's CIFAR-LR test accuracy is 76.27%; 77.87% is SOAP's. Same error for cross-entropy: "MuonW's 0.7054 and 77.9%" — MuonW's CE accuracy is 76.83%, 77.93% is Muon's. That numCifarCEBaselineAccMax is also 77.9 confirms the macro is the field max. The same macro is reused correctly two sentences later ("69.4% against 77.9%" as the field best), so it carries two meanings in one appendix.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit a separate `num{key}BestNameAcc` = the accuracy OF the loss-best method, and use it in the "against MuonW's …" sentences; keep `BestAcc` (= field max) only where the comparison is explicitly against the best accuracy in the field.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:692 (Appendix N, "Decreasing Memory Requirements", first sentence — unchanged black text)
findings.issue: "While the computational cost in the over-parametrized limit is only a factor of $k$ higher than SGD, the memory requirements can be significantly higher…" and "computing the Jacobian requires storing a number of model copies equal to the batch size". This is the exact claim the revision retires: the abstract, §1, §2.3, §5 and App. D all now state the cost is independent of $k$ and that the Jacobian is never formed, and CHANGES_v2 §2 lists "overhead is only a factor of k" under "Weakened or corrected … App. H". The sentence survived into App. N unedited and unmarked, so the paper contradicts itself and an unretracted retired claim is presented as current in black (i.e. as unchanged, already-reviewed text).
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite that opening in blue to match §2.3/App. D: the linear algebra is $k$-independent, the remaining cost is the capture, the micro-batch and mask knobs shrink what the capture must assemble. Keep the removed sentence as a `% OLD:` comment per the markup convention.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/sections_v2/app_spectra.tex:28 and :30 (¶"The floor", ¶"How the kept energy moves"), against tables_v2/spectra_mechanism.tex
findings.issue: Two causal claims are contradicted by the paper's own generated table. (a) "On three scans it is pinned at $100$\% throughout, because \texttt{rtol} sits below the round-off floor". The three 100% scans in tab:spectra-mechanism are MNIST-LR, CIFAR-LR and nanoGPT, all at rtol=1e-3, i.e. ABOVE the measured floor of 3.5e-4; and numSpectraRtolBelowFloor=1, so only ONE scan's rtol is below the floor. (b) ¶"The floor" says of that one scan "the cut is nominal: everything above the floor is kept, and the rank is set by $k$ or by the batch". The scan in question is Toy 1D (rtol=1e-4), which tab:spectra-mechanism records as "Binds: rtol" with used rank 4.2→14.4 out of $k=B=32$ and kept energy 92.08%→91.53% — the rank is set by rtol, not by $k$ or $B$, and nothing is pinned at 100%. Also at :26, "$k$ binds on \numSpectraKBinds{}" renders "k binds on 2", but the table's Binds column for those two scans reads "neither ($k=B$)".
findings.suggested_fix: Correct (a) to the measured reason (those scans have $k=B$ and no singular value below rtol·σ₁, so nothing above the floor is discarded); correct (b) to say that on Toy 1D the cut lands inside the round-off, so the rank is set by arithmetic rather than by the hyperparameter; and change "k binds on 2" to "neither cut binds on 2 ($k=B$)" to match the table.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:403 (§4.2) and sections_v2/app_spectra.tex:30
findings.issue: Self-contradictory claim, in the main text. §4.2: "The kept fraction of the batch residual \emph{rises} over training wherever the cut bites, from 92.3\% to 99.6\% on the polynomial scan, but falls on two scans, substantially so on CIFAR-10 cross-entropy." If it falls on two scans then it does not rise wherever the cut bites. App. O:30 carries the same defect: "On the two scans where the cut genuinely bites it \emph{rises}… On two it falls" — per tab:spectra-mechanism the cut bites on FOUR scans (Toy 1D, Polynomial, MNIST-CE, CIFAR-CE), rising on two and falling on two. "The two scans where the cut genuinely bites" is simply wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with the measured split: the cut discards nonzero energy on four of seven scans; kept energy rises on two (polynomial 92.3→99.6%, MNIST-CE 31→95.2%) and falls on two (1D 92.1→91.5%, CIFAR-CE 90.1→76.7%); it is pinned at 100% on the remaining three.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/figures_iclr/spectra/spectrum_truncation.pdf, panel (b) — Figure 25 on p71, cited from main text §4.2; caption at sections_v2/app_spectra.tex:50
findings.issue: Panel (b) "what the cut keeps" is the figure §4.2 points at for the kept-energy claim, and at printed size it shows exactly two distinguishable traces: a flat line at ~1.0 (five superimposed scans) and one black curve (MNIST-CE) rising from 0.3. CIFAR-CE — the single scan on which the kept energy falls substantially (90.1%→76.7%), the paper's most important caveat here — is not visible anywhere in the panel, and the polynomial rise (92.3→99.6%) and the 1D fall (92.1→91.5%) are invisible against a linear 0–1 axis. The caption also mismatches the content: it says panel (b) covers "the three headline scans and MNIST cross-entropy" (four scans) while the shared legend below the figure lists all seven. A reader who checks the caveat against the cited figure cannot find it.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw panel (b) as discarded fraction on a log axis (or zoom to 0.7–1.0), make sure CIFAR-CE is drawn and labelled, and correct the caption to name the scans actually plotted. Optionally split the flat-at-100% scans into a separate note so the four that bite are legible.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/sections_v2/app_cifar.tex:23 and :64 vs sections_v2/app_spectra.tex:26 and tables_v2/spectra_mechanism.tex
findings.issue: App. J and App. O give different, unreconciled used-rank numbers for the same two scans and draw opposite conclusions. App. J: CIFAR-LR "sits at 112 of the cap $k=128$ (87.9\%), so $k$ is close to binding and a larger $k$ might help"; CIFAR-CE "48.8 of 128 (38.1\%)". tab:spectra-mechanism: CIFAR-LR "Binds: rtol", used 128.0→81.6; CIFAR-CE used 106.0→36.6. So (i) App. J's premise that $k$ nearly binds on CIFAR-LR is contradicted by App. O's verdict that rtol binds there at the end of training (App. O:26 even says "on CIFAR-10 label regression neither binds at step 0 and \texttt{rtol} binds by the end"), which invalidates the drawn consequence "a larger $k$ might help"; (ii) 112 vs 81.6 and 48.8 vs 36.6 are an epoch-mean and a final-step value from two different modules (large_figs.sven_rank_used vs spectra_figs.mechanism_table) and the paper never says so.
findings.suggested_fix: State in App. J which statistic each number is ("mean over epochs" vs "final logged step") and cross-reference tab:spectra-mechanism; and either drop "a larger $k$ might help" or qualify it with what actually binds at the end of the CIFAR-LR run.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:373 (§4, baselines paragraph) and :111 (abstract)
findings.issue: "The field is \numNMethodsMlp{} methods on the perceptron scans: SGD, SGD with momentum, RMSprop, Adam, AdamW, SGD with the Polyak step size, stochastic limited-memory BFGS, SOAP, Shampoo, K-FAC, Muon and MuonW, and the two methods mechanistically closest to Sven, HIG and JD" renders "15 methods" followed by exactly 14 names (Sven is the 15th but is not in the list). Worse, the sentence blankets all four perceptron scans, while tab:ranking gives field size n=15 for 1D and polynomial but n=14 for both MNIST scans, and §4.1 then quotes ranks out of 14 ("3 of 14", "4 of 14"). The reason (K-FAC has no eligible MNIST configuration — all 40 runs fail on each scan) lives only in App. P. The abstract's "a field of fifteen optimizers" reads as 15 baselines plus Sven.
findings.suggested_fix: Write "Sven and 14 baselines" (or "a field of 15 including Sven"), and add the half-sentence that K-FAC drops out of both MNIST scans, which is why those fields are 14.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:415-416 (§4.1), :363 (Fig. 1 caption), :427 (Limitations), :353 (§3)
findings.issue: The prose names only MuonW as ahead of Sven on MNIST, but tab:ranking has Sven 3rd on MNIST-LR (MuonW 1st, HIG 2nd) and 4th on MNIST-CE (MuonW 1st, Muon 2nd, HIG 3rd). "3 of 14 and 4 of 14 behind MuonW", the Fig. 1 caption "HIG leads the polynomial task and MuonW MNIST", and the Limitations "HIG leads both synthetic regressions and MuonW both MNIST" all leave the reader to infer Sven is runner-up. §3:353 compounds this: "HIG is also the strongest baseline on both of our synthetic regression scans, where it finishes ahead of Sven" — HIG in fact finishes ahead of Sven on ALL FOUR perceptron scans (tab:headline MNIST-LR: HIG 0.05298 vs Sven 0.05328), and HIG is drawn above Sven in the MNIST panel of Fig. 1, so the figure shows what the caption does not say.
findings.suggested_fix: State the ranks with the methods above Sven named: "3 of 14 behind MuonW and HIG on MNIST label regression, 4 of 14 behind MuonW, Muon and HIG on cross-entropy". In §3 change "on both of our synthetic regression scans" to "on all four perceptron scans".

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:353 (§3) vs sections_v2/app_cifar.tex:15, tables_v2/ranking.tex note, sections_v2/app_exp_details.tex:314
findings.issue: §3 gives one reason for HIG's absence — "because it decomposes the output Jacobian, its cost grows with the output dimension, which is why it appears only on the perceptron scans" — and App. C:314 repeats it. But App. J:15 says "…and the reason HIG cannot be run at all" is batch-statistics BatchNorm, and tab:ranking's own note says "HIG refuses batch-statistics normalisation". Two different single causes are asserted for the same omission in three places; cost explains the language models, BatchNorm explains CIFAR-10.
findings.suggested_fix: Give both reasons once (cost for the language models, batch-coupled normalisation for ResNet18) and cross-reference, rather than asserting a single cause in each location.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:427 (Limitations) and iclr_manuscript/CHANGES_v2.md line 115
findings.issue: The Limitations ratio mixes measurement sources without saying so: "\numCifarLRSvenMsStep{}~ms against \numProfCifarAdamMsStep{}~ms on ResNet18" = 177 ms vs 23.7 ms, where 177 is headline.efficiency_table (the campaign's standalone timing pass at the selected configuration) and 23.7 is profile_helpers.method_table (the synthetic profile at its own set point). App. Q's own opening paragraph explicitly warns that "the absolute milliseconds here are not the wall-clock numbers of Table \ref{tab:headline}" and that "where the two are quoted together, the source of each is named" — which this sentence does not do. The profile's like-for-like ratio is 7.89× (tab:profile_methods). Separately, CHANGES_v2 §1 §5 claims the limitations paragraph says "27× on ResNet18"; nothing in the tex supports 27×, the numbers give 7.5×.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote both numbers from one pass (either the timing pass's Sven and Adam, or the profile's 188 ms / 23.7 ms = 7.89×) and name the source in-line; fix the 27× in CHANGES_v2.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:212 (§2.1 dimensions paragraph) vs :480 (App. A), :527 and :611 (App. B); claim at iclr_manuscript/CHANGES_v2.md line 219
findings.issue: §2.1 defines "$N$ for the size of the training set" and uses $P$ for parameters throughout the main text and every generated table. Appendix A:480 writes "$\{\theta^i:i=1\ldots N\}$ are our parameters" and Appendix B:527 "parameters $\theta = (\theta^i)$, where $i=1\ldots N$", and B:611 "if the batch size $|B|$ is greater or equal than the number of parameters $N$" — i.e. $N$ = parameter count and $|B|$ = batch size, the exact opposite convention. CHANGES_v2 §3.5 asserts "Appendices A and B keep their own $N$ for the parameter count, and §2 says so"; §2 does not say so anywhere. A reader of App. B:611 will read "batch size ≥ number of parameters $N$" against a main text where $N$ is 50,000 MNIST images.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one blue sentence at §2.1:212 ("Appendices A and B, which are unchanged, write $N$ for the parameter count and $|B|$ for the batch size") or rename the symbols in A/B. Either way correct the CHANGES_v2 claim.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:369 and :394; sections_v2/app_additional.tex:21 and :50; sections_v2/app_mnist_ce.tex:16; sections_v2/app_fig5.tex:15; sections_v2/app_kappa.tex:13
findings.issue: Seven passages refer to an uncitable prior version of the paper — "the headline task of the earlier version of this work" (main text §4), "MNIST is no longer the wash we previously reported" (main text §4.1), "this retires the single-seed comparison of the earlier version of this work", "An earlier version of this work reported that $\kappa = 1$ was unusable", "the impression given by an earlier version of this study". The paper is typeset "Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2026" with "Anonymous authors / Paper under double-blind review", and CHANGES_v2 §3.4 records the integrator's decision that this is "a fresh submission, not a response letter" (all "R1 asked…" phrasings were removed for that reason). Pointing an anonymous reviewer at an unnamed earlier version of the same work is both inconsistent with that decision and a double-blind risk, and PAPER_CONTRACTS says the paper "simply describes the protocol that was run" rather than the campaign's history.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite each as a statement about the measurement rather than about a prior draft ("a $k$ sweep taken at one conservative \texttt{rtol} measures the interaction of the two cuts", "with signed residuals all 210 runs complete at $\kappa\in\{1,2,3\}$", "a single-seed reading of this scan would suggest the field is a wash; at five seeds the ordering is resolved"), or make it an explicit citation if the authors intend to reference the prior version.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/iclr2026_conference_v2.tex §4 (pp. 7-9): only floats are Figure 1 (p7) and Algorithm 1 (p3)
findings.issue: The results section contains no table and no second figure. Every headline number is prose only, and §4 cites "Table 15 in Appendix E" (p32), "Fig. 25" (p71) and "Fig. 39 in Appendix Q" (p83) — forward references of 23 to 75 pages from page 8. A reviewer reading the 9-page main text cannot see the comparison being claimed, which sits badly with the user's priority that the paper contain "a comprehensive summary of all results obtained" and that new baselines appear "as new lines on main-text plots". The integrator flags this as the layout's weakest point (CHANGES_v2 §3.3) and says Table 1 is one `\input` from returning.
findings.suggested_fix: Recover ~0.5 page (the §2.2/§2.3 blue paragraphs and the §4 protocol paragraph are the most compressible) and put `tables_v2/headline_confirm_compact.tex` back in §4 as Table 1, or at minimum move `fig:cost_memory` into §4 so the efficiency claim has a main-text figure.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/figures_iclr/main/headline_curves.pdf (Figure 1, p7, middle column) and figures_iclr/main/headline_curves_all.pdf (Figure 2, p47, middle column)
findings.issue: Both MNIST panels are dominated by outliers and cannot support the claims made about them. In Fig. 2 SOAP's failed selected configuration (val 0.5808 ± 0.44, 44.5% accuracy) draws a band spanning 0.2–1.0 that fills the panel while the other 13 methods are compressed into an unreadable 0.05–0.07 sliver; in both figures the wall-time panel is stretched to 10^3 s by HIG's 58.3 s/epoch, leaving every other curve as a short segment in the left margin. §4.1 claims Sven beats Adam and AdamW on MNIST by a resolved paired margin (0.0533 vs 0.0584); that difference is invisible at printed size in the figure the reader is sent to.
findings.suggested_fix: Clip or inset the MNIST loss axis (e.g. 0.045–0.12 with a broken axis or a zoom inset), and either clip the time axis or mark HIG and SOAP as off-scale with their values annotated.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/figures_iclr/spectra/spectrum_truncation.pdf panel (c) (Figure 25, p71); caption sections_v2/app_spectra.tex:50; prose iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:403 and app_spectra.tex:26
findings.issue: §4.2 and App. O quote "the rank inverted is \numPolySvenUsedRankFirst{} at the first logged step and \numPolySvenUsedRankFinal{} at the last" = 7 → 13.4, and tab:spectra-mechanism gives Toy 1D 4.2 → 14.4. Panel (c) is drawn with a 60-step moving average, so the polynomial (red) curve starts at ≈13 and ends at ≈11.5 and the 1D (blue) curve starts at ≈14 — neither the quoted first-step values nor the rising trend is recoverable from the figure, and the red curve appears to fall where the text says it rises. Panel (a) has the same problem in a smaller way: its in-axes legend prints "step 6,220" in yellow on white, which is close to illegible at printed size, and the "$k=16$" label is red text on the red $k$ line.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the caption that the quoted first/last-step values are unsmoothed and that panel (c) is a 60-step moving average, or overlay the unsmoothed first and last points. Recolour the panel-(a) legend text to a dark hue and move the "$k=16$" label off the line.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/ Overleaf-readiness — iclr2026_conference_v2.tex:21,26,34 (algpseudocode, bbm, nicefrac) vs campaign/PAPER_CONTRACTS.md lines 49-52
findings.issue: The contract requires the v2 file to compile "from inside iclr_manuscript/ with pdflatex … with no errors". It does not: a clean copy of iclr_manuscript/ with no TEXINPUTS fails on pass 1 with `! LaTeX Error: File 'algpseudocode.sty' not found. … Fatal error occurred, no output PDF file produced`. The 92-page clean build I reproduced needs three out-of-repo stubs in agent_lab/paper_build/shim/. The three packages are inherited unchanged from iclr2026_conference.tex and are standard on Overleaf, so this is pre-existing and CHANGES_v2 lines 29-34 disclose it honestly — but it means the local proof PDF is not the Overleaf layout: the shim maps `\State`→`\STATE`, `\Require`→`\REQUIRE` etc. via `algorithmic`, so Algorithms 1-4 (including the new Algorithm 2, alg:gram) will render differently, at a different height, on Overleaf. Algorithm 2 sits on p29 with tab:gram_cost; a height change there can reflow App. D.
findings.suggested_fix: Compile once on Overleaf (or on a TeX Live with algorithmicx/bbm/nicefrac) before the authors trust the page count, and re-check the main-text page count and the four algorithm floats there. Do not vendor the stubs into iclr_manuscript/ — they would shadow the real packages.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/sections_v2/app_robustness.tex:264 (Figure 38 caption, p83)

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/sections_v2/app_profiling.tex:42 (Figure 40 caption, p85)
findings.issue: Caption says "A cell without a measurement names the reason instead of going blank", but the Sven(hooks)/ResNet18 cells print "--" with no reason, and HIG's nanoGPT and ResNet18 cells print "inf.", which in a ratio heatmap reads as an infinite ratio rather than "infeasible" (tab:profile_methods uses the clearer note "infeasible"). findings.location: iclr_manuscript/figures_iclr/spectra/spectrum_truncation.pdf, panel (c) y-axis label (Figure 25, p71); same label in figures_iclr/spectra/online_mechanism.pdf
findings.issue: The y axis reads "SVs inverted $\min(k,\ \texttt{rtol})$". That expression is wrong: it takes the minimum of a rank and a relative tolerance. Equation (\ref{eqn:rank_law}) and the algorithm both define it as $\min(k,\ \#\{i:\sigma_i \ge \texttt{rtol}\cdot\sigma_1\})$, which the text abbreviates as "$\min(k, \texttt{rtol}\text{-rank})$".
findings.suggested_fix: Change the axis label to "SVs inverted, $\min(k,\ \texttt{rtol}\text{-rank})$" in analysis/paper_assets/spectra.py.

findings.location: iclr_manuscript/tables_v2/confirmation_{toy_1d_scan,polynomial_scan,mnist_scan_labelRegression,mnist_scan_ce}.tex — the K-FAC "Selected configuration" cell

summary:
The build is clean and the numbers layer is sound, but the paper ships six substantive claim errors and one broken toolchain promise, so it is not ready.

BUILD (verified in a scratch copy of iclr_manuscript/, pdflatex → bibtex → pdflatex ×2, TeX Live 2018): 0 errors, 0 undefined references, 0 undefined citations, 0 duplicate labels, 92 pages, worst overfull box 8.97 pt (4 instances). Main text is 9 pages — sec:code ends p9, references start p10 — so it is exactly at the ICLR limit. bibtex emits 4 benign warnings (empty author/year on lecun1998mnist, undefined entry type for the TorchVision entry). Appendix lettering is A–R with app:kappaScans = M, matching the plan.
